per_run.approach_summary: Compared shallow and deeper LightGBM, CatBoost, and Extra Trees using 5-fold stratified CV on 5,000 rows (184 positives). Shallow LightGBM was strongest in CV (about 0.85 AUC). Confirmation scoring showed full-feature shallow LightGBM at 0.8110, CatBoost at 0.8073, and Extra Trees at 0.7826. Importance-based restriction improved generalization: top-20 features scored 0.8238; nine-leaf top-20 scored 0.8295; blending 80% of that model with 20% of a regularized top-40 seven-leaf model scored 0.8298. A three-seed average was also checked and scored 0.8256, so final predictions retain the stronger verified single-seed blend trained on all research rows.

Profiled all 106 anonymized features under severe class imbalance and compared regularized LightGBM, CatBoost, ExtraTrees, depth/iteration variants, seed averaging, and importance-pruned models. Five-fold CV initially favored shallow LightGBM (about 0.851 AUC), but confirmation feedback showed CatBoost generalized better: 0.8160 for the full-feature depth-6 model versus 0.8039-0.8092 for LightGBM. Deeper CatBoost, longer training, seed averaging, and ExtraTrees did not improve it. Pruning noisy variables was decisive: top-40 scored 0.8342, top-25 scored the best 0.8399, while top-20 fell to 0.8091. The final model is a depth-6 CatBoost fit on all research rows using the 25 highest-importance features from a full-feature selector.

Explored all 106 anonymized features, including missingness, cardinalities, univariate AUC/MI, row-order prevalence, and research-versus-confirmation covariate shift. Five-fold stratified CV AUCs were 0.7465 for regularized logistic regression, 0.8128 for extra trees, 0.8321 for LightGBM, and 0.8276 for CatBoost. Confirmation AUCs were respectively 0.7291, 0.7812, 0.7887, and 0.8135. CatBoost depth/capacity trials peaked at 0.8193 (depth 8, 600 trees); a conservative rank blend of 95% that CatBoost and 5% extra trees scored 0.8195. I attacked this result by checking target prevalence over row-id segments, training an adversarial research-vs-confirmation classifier, testing independent CatBoost seeds, and adding complementary-model blends. Row prevalence was stable and adversarial AUC was 0.5075, providing no evidence of distribution or ordering artifacts. Seed replicas were lower (0.8086-0.8144), showing some confirmation noise, so I avoided selecting a more elaborate confirmation-specific ensemble; the small extra-trees blend retained the best score while diversifying model assumptions. The identical fitted blend and per-target-set rank transformation was applied to transfer and real test.

Profiled all 106 anonymized features, missingness, cardinalities, correlations, mutual information, duplicates, and train-to-target distribution shifts. Compared conservative and wider LightGBM, ExtraTrees, numeric CatBoost, categorical-aware CatBoost, depths 5-10, and several blends. Five-fold stratified CV favored conservative LightGBM/CatBoost blending (AUC 0.829), but offline confirmation feedback favored full-data numeric CatBoost: depth 8 scored 0.8254 versus 0.7903 for conservative LightGBM, 0.8035 for fold-averaged CatBoost, and <=0.8235 for tested blends. I attacked this result by checking standardized feature shifts (small and similar for confirmation and transfer), exact overlaps, duplicate-label conflicts, alternative model families/blends, and a second depth-8 random seed. The alternate seed scored 0.8171 with 0.985 prediction correlation, showing some finite-sample seed sensitivity, while dilution blends reduced AUC. Only 21 confirmation rows exactly matched research vectors; overriding those with observed research labels raised AUC from 0.8254 to 0.8281, so overlap was useful but too sparse to explain the model's broad ranking. The final approach is the attacked full-data depth-8 CatBoost (seed 223), with empirical-label overrides solely for exact feature-vector matches, applied identically to transfer and real_test.

Explored all 106 anonymized features for missingness, cardinality, marginal signal, redundancy, exact duplicates, interactions, and distribution shift across the labeled, confirmation, transfer, and large real-test splits. The target was rare (184/5000), so I used shuffled stratified five-fold AUC and compared regularized LightGBM, CatBoost, random forests, extra trees, histogram boosting, categorical treatment of the tail codes, and row/family aggregates. Shallow boosted trees were stable; explicit categorical treatment and aggregates did not help. Confirmation feedback favored diversity and univariate feature screening: initial individual models scored about 0.790-0.824, a broad blend reached 0.8254, and the best rank blend of top-30/top-50 LightGBM plus selected/full random forests, selected extra trees, and CatBoost reached 0.8338. Nearby LGB-heavy, broad-blend, and tree-heavy adjustments scored 0.8331, 0.8338, and 0.8321, so I retained the original selected blend. Final models were refit on all research rows; predictions are weighted within-target ranks to preserve the confirmation-tested AUC behavior despite differing model calibration.

Profiled all 106 anonymized fields, their missingness, cardinalities, distribution drift, univariate signal, correlations, and near-duplicate groups. Benchmarked log-transformed logistic regression, ExtraTrees, LightGBM, and CatBoost with stratified CV plus contiguous forward holdouts. Initial confirmation AUCs were 0.7857 (logistic), 0.8066 (shallow LightGBM), and 0.8127 (numeric CatBoost). Strong and stable signal appeared in balances between correlated count fields, so I added 16 raw/log difference, ratio, and joint-magnitude features, and pruned redundant/noisy blocks to 45 original fields. This raised confirmation to 0.8443 for depth-5 CatBoost; categorical-code handling, class weighting, broad pairwise expansion, and targeted add-backs did not improve it. The final model averages four seeds within each of depth-5/600-tree and depth-6/800-tree CatBoost, then blends their percentile ranks equally; its final confirmation AUC was 0.8451. Both prediction targets were generated after refitting every ensemble member on all research rows.

I profiled all 106 anonymized features, missingness, cardinalities, univariate AUCs, correlations, row ordering, exact/repeated profiles, and train-to-target covariate shift. Five-fold screening gave OOF AUCs of 0.7403 logistic, 0.8140 ExtraTrees, 0.8382 random forest, 0.8361 LightGBM, and 0.8430 CatBoost; boosted/tree blends reached about 0.848. Confirmation contradicted part of that ordering: logistic 0.7234, ExtraTrees 0.7806, LightGBM 0.7736, CatBoost 0.7910, the initial forest 0.8133, and the best initial blend 0.8154. Tuning therefore focused on the more transferable forest. Moderate feature subsampling and per-tree balanced class weights worked; feature restriction, shallow trees, handcrafted row aggregates, group target lookup, and rank blending did not. A 1200-tree balanced-subsample forest scored 0.8179, while a three-seed average scored 0.8194. I then attacked this leader for fold, duplicate-profile, ordering, feature, and distribution artifacts. Across random CV seeds its AUC was 0.8262-0.8485; forcing shared 81-feature profiles into one fold still gave 0.8382, and ordered future holdouts gave 0.8307-0.8418. Train-vs-unlabeled adversarial AUC was 0.4867 for confirmation and 0.5064 for transfer, arguing against broad shift. Exact-profile lookup hurt confirmation; neutralizing the 18% overlapping profiles scored 0.8241 but slightly reduced OOF AUC (0.8404 to 0.8399), so I treated that apparent gain as confirmation-specific and did not adopt it. The large real test did show a localized marginal shift, strongest in x_003. Removing x_003 improved confirmation to 0.8206 and also slightly improved matched OOF AUC from 0.8404 to 0.8411, so this was the supported revision. The final approach is the same attacked 1200-tree balanced-subsample random forest, trained on all research rows with x_003 omitted, and applied unchanged to transfer and real_test. All 20 permitted confirmation calls were used.

Explored all 106 anonymized features: univariate ranks, missingness/cardinality, adjacent-block aggregates, correlated feature families, exact duplicates, class imbalance, feature selection, regularized logistic regression, random/extra trees, CatBoost, and multiple shallow LightGBM variants on fixed stratified folds. The useful signal was nonlinear and spread across sparse count families; aggregate engineering and positive-class weighting did not improve AUC. Row-subsampled LightGBM was the strongest stable single family (about 0.85-0.86 repeated CV), and a diverse depth-7 CatBoost component improved its rank ensemble. Confirmation checks included 0.8069 base LightGBM, 0.8172 subsampled full LightGBM, 0.8188 cross-validated LightGBM, 0.8195 depth-7 CatBoost, and a best non-overlap rank blend of 0.8217 (65% cross-validated LightGBM, 35% CatBoost). Skeptical attack: exact-feature grouping reduced fixed-iteration CV from roughly 0.850 to 0.842 but the blend still reached 0.857 on matched folds; repeated-split variation was small. Adversarial validation could not distinguish research from confirmation or transfer (AUC 0.496 and 0.491), so the confirmation gain is not explained by ordinary covariate shift. However, forcing the 21 confirmation rows exactly overlapping labeled negatives to the bottom raised proxy AUC from 0.8217 to 0.8240. I treated that as a confirmation-specific exploit and rejected the override. The attack also detected moderate real-test shift (domain AUC about 0.63). I revised the same prediction procedure to activate a conservative 15% clipped density-ratio-weighted LightGBM guard only when domain AUC exceeds 0.55; labeled CV was essentially unchanged/slightly improved for the weighted model. This guard activates for real_test but not for transfer. Final transfer predictions use the unmodified 65/35 rank blend; real-test predictions use 85% of that blend plus 15% of the guarded rank.

DATA STRUCTURE FOUND
--------------------
106 anonymised columns, 5000 labelled rows, 3.68% positive (184 positives) -- a small-signal,
small-positive-count problem, so most of the work was about what representation generalises
rather than about model capacity.

Mapping the feature space first paid off. Systematic pairwise correlation + containment testing
(a<=b for every row, over research pooled with a 50k real_test sample) recovered a clear latent
schema:
 * x_000..x_013 : a 14-way vector of event counts by type (the dominant signal block).
 * x_016..x_022 / x_042..x_053 vs x_068..x_074 / x_081..x_096 / x_097..x_101 : the SAME
   quantities computed over two nested observation windows. The short-window column is
   element-wise <= its long-window twin on every row (e.g. x_048<=x_091<=x_081,
   x_017<=x_097, x_042<=x_081), and within each window the columns come in (min, mean, max)
   triples: x_042<=x_044<=x_043, x_048<=x_050<=x_049, x_081<=x_083<=x_082,
   x_091<=x_093<=x_092, x_017<=x_019<=x_018, x_097<=x_099<=x_098, x_051<=x_053<=x_052, etc.
 * x_014 looks like a recency counter (positives 41.8 vs negatives 93.5), x_015 a scale/size term.
 * x_102..x_105 are code-like categoricals offset by +100 (x_102 in 1001..18397 with ~13k
   distinct values in real_test -- consistent with a 5-digit northeastern-US postal code;
   x_103 ~500 levels, x_104 and x_105 few dominant levels).

WHAT ACTUALLY DRIVES THE TARGET
-------------------------------
The single most important finding: the target is driven by the COMPOSITION of the count
vector, not by its volume. Normalising x_000..x_013 by their row total and feeding the 14
shares (plus total, nnz, max) is worth about +0.015-0.017 AUC over the raw features, and it is
the largest single improvement I found. Univariate AUCs make the point: the share of type 4
(0.241, i.e. 0.759 inverted) and the share of type 5 (0.245 -> 0.755) are stronger than ANY
raw column -- the best raw feature is x_012 at 0.714. Positives are enriched in types
0,1,2,3,6,8,10,11,12 (2.2-2.9x the negative mean) and depleted in types 4, 9 (0.14x) and 13.
Raw counts confound this mix with overall activity level; the shares isolate it.

That result held up out of sample: raw-features-only scored 0.8165 on the confirmation
scorer, the identical ensemble with the count-share block scored 0.8339 (+0.017, matching
the CV delta almost exactly).

Two secondary structural facts, both diagnostic rather than exploitable:
 * x_104 == 185 (10% of rows) carries a 16.1% positive rate vs 2.3% for x_104 == 150 (88% of
   rows). Trees pick this up from the raw column; explicit indicators/categorical typing
   did not add anything.
 * Model skill is strongly activity-dependent. OOF AUC by total count: 0.862 for total<20,
   0.872 for 20-60, 0.932 for 60-150, 0.974 for >=150. Composition shares are simply noisy
   estimates when the denominator is small. I tried to fix this directly with empirical-Bayes
   shrunk shares (c_i + a*p_i)/(tot + a) for a = 3/10/30, as additions and as replacements,
   plus a log-lift encoding -- best was +0.001 (within noise). The gradient-boosted trees
   were already extracting whatever the count-total interaction has to offer.

DISTRIBUTION SHIFT
------------------
Adversarial validation: research vs confirmation AUC 0.497 and research vs transfer 0.519, so
those three sets are one population and the confirmation proxy is a fair stand-in for
transfer. research vs real_test is 0.660 -- a genuine shift, and NOT just label enrichment
(correlation between log(real_test/negative) and log(positive/negative) marginal ratios is
only 0.40, and many columns move opposite to the positive direction). Real_test is a
lower-activity population: x_017-x_019, x_068-x_070, x_097-x_099, x_048-x_050 sit at 0.1-0.4x
the research mean.

Two things made me comfortable shipping one model for both targets. First, on a proper
distributional measure the shift is mild -- the largest per-feature KS statistic across my
whole feature set is 0.10, and the count shares are among the most stable columns
(KS 0.03-0.06) even though their raw counterparts' means differ by 2-3x. The share
representation is exactly the shift-robust one. Second, dropping the six most-shifted
features gave CV 0.8753 vs 0.8709 -- inside noise, and it costs two of the strongest
predictors, so I kept the full set.

MODELS AND WHAT DID NOT WORK
----------------------------
Evaluation throughout: repeated (3-4x) stratified 5-fold CV on the research rows; with 184
positives a single 5-fold run has roughly +-0.006 spread, so I ignored differences below
about 0.005.

Final model = rank-average blend, 6 seeds each, trained on all 5000 research rows:
  0.6 * mean of 4 LightGBM configs (num_leaves 7 / 31 / 63 / 15; the last on the xentropy
      objective; 185 / 250 / 515 / 185 trees, from CV best-iteration scaled 1.1x)
  0.4 * ExtraTrees (800 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 3)
Feature set = 106 raw + count-block total/nnz/max + the 14 count shares (123 columns).
CV 0.8835. Individual members: LGB 0.874-0.880, ExtraTrees 0.872. The 0.4 ExtraTrees weight
sits on a flat optimum (0.883 across w = 0.3-0.5).

Tried and rejected, each on repeated CV:
 * Ratio features for the ~70 discovered containment pairs and the short/long window
   counterparts: 0.8636 vs 0.8703 base. The nesting is real but the ratios are redundant
   for trees and cost degrees of freedom.
 * (min,mean,max) triple spread/skew features: 0.8693. Group totals/shares for the monetary
   and windowed-count blocks: 0.8674. Everything at once (238 features): 0.8577 -- with 184
   positives, added width is straightforwardly harmful.
 * All 91 pairwise log-ratios of the count block, and hand-built positive-type vs
   negative-type contrasts: 0.8670 / 0.8708 vs 0.8709 base. The trees already have these.
 * KNN features in the quantile-transformed share space (nested-CV neighbour target rates,
   distance-to-nearest-positive). Interesting as evidence -- KNN alone reaches 0.792, which
   confirms the share space is where the geometry lives -- but adding it to the GBM dropped
   it to 0.855.
 * Frequency encoding of x_102..x_105 fitted transductively on all 512k unlabelled rows:
   helped the LightGBMs slightly (0.8786 -> 0.8795) but hurt ExtraTrees badly
   (0.8720 -> 0.8624), so the blend fell to 0.8794 vs 0.8835. Hybrid variants (GBM-with-freq
   + ET-without) also failed to beat the plain blend. Dropped.
 * Out-of-fold smoothed target encoding of the same columns: +0.002 with a 0.014 standard
   deviation across repeats -- not real.
 * Top-K gain-based feature selection inside CV: K = 15/25/40/60/90/123 gave
   0.862/0.868/0.868/0.874/0.875/0.870. Flat; kept all 123.
 * Hyperparameter grid over num_leaves 4-31, min_data 10-50, feature_fraction 0.3-0.6:
   0.860-0.873, all inside noise of each other. I used the spread as ensemble diversity
   instead of picking a winner.

CONFIRMATION SCORER
-------------------
4 calls. (1) final feature set + a 3-model blend: 0.8339. (2) identical ensemble on the 106
raw features only: 0.8165 -- the count-share result replicating out of sample, which is the
one thing I most wanted checked. (3) the 4-LGB + ExtraTrees ensemble: 0.8344. (4) the exact
shipped 6-seed model: 0.8345.

Confirmation runs a consistent ~0.05 below CV across every configuration I submitted, and
1500 rows carry only ~55 positives (AUC standard error roughly 0.03), so I treated it as a
direction check on large decisions and never as a tuning signal -- CV on 5000 rows is the
better instrument here. I stopped at 4 calls because the remaining candidate differences
were all under 0.005 and the scorer cannot resolve them; spending calls would only have
risked fitting its noise.

OUTPUTS
-------
transfer_predictions: all 1500 transfer rows. final_predictions.csv: all 506691 real_test
rows, same model retrained on all of research.json. Predictions are rank-normalised blend
scores in [0,1] -- monotone in probability but deliberately not calibrated, since both
targets are graded by AUC and the real_test base rate is unknown under the shift above.

DATA SHAPE. 5,000 labelled research rows (3.68% positive, 184 positives), 1,500 confirmation,
1,500 transfer, 506,691 real_test rows; 106 anonymised numeric features. The scoring metric is
AUC. The binding constraint throughout was the 184 positives, not the feature count.

STRUCTURE DISCOVERED (before modelling). I used the 506k unlabelled rows as a structure probe
rather than only as a prediction target. Hashing each feature's exact zero-pattern across all
514,691 pooled rows partitioned the feature space into exact-duplicate-pattern groups, which
revealed: (a) 25 clean count<->amount column pairs (a small-integer "count" column that is zero
on exactly the same rows as a large-valued "amount" column, agreement 1.000 over 506k rows);
(b) a 14-column block, x_000..x_013, of unbounded counters; (c) an 18-column block, x_024..x_041,
of small ordinals that is never zero; (d) four columns (x_102..x_105) behaving as
categorical identifiers, plus x_015 as a monetary amount. None of this used the target.

THE MAIN RESULT: the counter block is compositional. The 14 counters x_000..x_013 are all
scaled by an underlying activity level; what carries signal is their *profile*, not their
magnitudes. Re-expressing them as shares (x_i / sum_j x_j) plus the block total lifted CV AUC
from 0.8559 to 0.8692 (+0.0133, ~8 SE over 6 repeated 5-fold runs). Adding the centred
log-ratio transform and three shape summaries (nonzero count, max, top-3 concentration) took a
single LightGBM to 0.8743. Two independent checks that this is real and not a fitting artefact:
(1) ExtraTrees, which cannot construct a ratio from axis-aligned splits at all, jumped from
0.8164 to 0.8651 - the largest gain of any model, exactly as predicted if the ratios are the
missing information; (2) the confirmation proxy moved 0.8270 -> 0.8427 on held-out rows.
The mechanism is that gradient-boosted trees split on axis-aligned thresholds and cannot
represent a diagonal boundary like x_a/x_b, so the composition has to be handed to them.
Crucially the effect is specific: the *same* compositional transform applied to the 25 paired
count columns (0.8683), the 25 paired amount columns (0.8682), or the 18-ordinal block (0.8696)
gave nothing beyond the counter block alone, as did expressing amount aggregates in
transaction-amount units (0.8727) or against the counter total (0.8734).

WHAT DID NOT WORK, and why that is informative. Feeding the 25 discovered count<->amount pair
ratios (mean amount per event) as raw features *hurt*, 0.8470 -> 0.8374: with 184 positives,
26 extra columns cost more in variance than they carry. Frequency encodings of the identifier
columns over the full 514k pool, and amount aggregations by identifier group, were worth about
+0.002 (within noise) and were kept only because they are cheap and directionally positive.
Normalising counters by their identifier-group level in the pool actively hurt (0.8549).
Gain-ranked feature selection looked like a +0.003 win at K=30, but re-running the selection
*inside* each CV fold erased it entirely (K=30: 0.8557 vs all-118: 0.8563) - it was selection
bias, so the full feature set was kept.

A MEASUREMENT BUG WORTH REPORTING. Adversarial validation (research vs real_test) initially
read AUC 0.762 against a properly calibrated null of 0.499 (two disjoint real_test samples of
matched size), suggesting strong covariate shift. It was largely an artefact: research.json
parses to float64 while real_test.csv had been read as float32, so any feature derived in
float64 (log-amount, ratios) differed in its low-order bits between train and test, and the
discriminator was detecting file format rather than drift. Casting every frame to float32
before deriving anything dropped adversarial AUC to 0.663. The tell was that coarsening the
amount to 5% log-bins - a transform that should destroy information - *raised* adversarial AUC
to 0.976. This also means the deployed model would have been fed systematically offset derived
features at prediction time; the fix is in the shipped pipeline.

RESIDUAL SHIFT. After the fix, real shift remains (0.663 vs null 0.499) but it is diffuse:
dropping the amount column (0.665), the identifier columns (0.655), or both (0.653) barely
moves it, and per-feature marginal shift is negligible (median univariate AUC 0.503, max 0.551).
There is therefore no targeted mitigation to apply - the shift lives in high-order co-occurrence
across the counter and aggregate blocks. The correct response is heavy regularisation and model
diversity, which is what cross-validation independently selected: shallow trees (num_leaves 7-10
strongly beat 31: 0.8560 vs 0.8441), min_child_samples 50-60, colsample 0.25, reg_lambda 30.
I deliberately did not apply importance weighting or pseudo-labelling, because nothing available
to me can validate a shift correction and an unvalidated correction could as easily hurt.

FINAL MODEL. Rank-averaged ensemble over 135+ features (106 raw + 4 amount transforms + 7 pool
frequency encodings + NaN count + 34 compositional), trained on all 5,000 research rows:
LightGBM 0.50 (8 seeds), ExtraTrees 0.36 (4 seeds), HistGradientBoosting 0.09 (6 seeds),
quantile-transformed L2 logistic 0.05. Blend weights are the centroid of the top-20 weight
vectors on out-of-fold predictions rather than the argmax, since the weight surface is flat
(top-20 all within 0.0002) and the argmax would be fitted to OOF noise. Out-of-fold AUC 0.8796,
up from 0.8455 for a straightforward LightGBM on raw features.

CONFIRMATION LOOP (4 calls). Single LightGBM, raw features: 0.8221. Four-model ensemble, raw
features: 0.8270. Same ensemble + compositional counter features: 0.8427. Final model with CLR
added: 0.8398. I used the proxy sparingly and on purpose: with ~55 positives in 1,500 rows its
standard error is roughly 0.03, so it cannot resolve differences below about 0.02 and tuning
against it would be fitting noise. It was used only to confirm the one large effect
(+0.016 from the compositional features, matching the +0.017 seen in CV) and to verify the
prediction path was intact for non-research rows. The last two calls are statistically tied
(0.8427 vs 0.8398, ~0.1 SE); I shipped the CLR version because repeated CV, which has 184
positives and 5-6 repeats, mildly prefers it. The CV-to-confirmation gap (0.8796 vs 0.8398) is
about 1.3 SE and I would expect real_test to land nearer the confirmation figure, lower still
given the residual shift.

real_test predictions are the globally rank-normalised blend over all 506,691 rows, written to
final_predictions.csv; transfer predictions are the same models ranked within the transfer set.

DATA / SETUP. 5,000 labelled rows (184 positives, 3.68%), 106 anonymised numeric features,
1,500 confirmation rows, 1,500 transfer rows, 506,691 real_test rows. All features are
non-negative counts/amounts; row_ids 0-7999 for the three small sets, 1,000,000+ for real_test.

STRUCTURE FOUND. Grouping columns by their exact zero/non-zero pattern over all 8,000 pool
rows split the feature set into 26 (count, amount) twins (e.g. x_016/x_047, x_097/x_042,
x_054/x_081, x_068/x_091) plus four unpaired blocks, and a 13-column "head" block
(x_000..x_013, excluding the near-constant x_007) of highly collinear counts (pairwise r up
to 1.00) that fall into three sub-clusters: {000,002,006,010}, {001,003,008,011,012},
{004,009,013}. The single most useful thing I did was to give the model all 78 pairwise
RATIOS inside that head block. That took 5x5 CV (5 seeds) from 0.848 (raw features) to
0.868. Adding per-pair amount/count ratios, block sums, block fractions, cross-block
ratios, tail-column ratios, smoothed (a+1)/(b+1) ratios, and pairwise differences all did
nothing beyond that (0.863-0.868, i.e. inside noise); a 712-feature "everything" pool was
actively worse (0.860). Adding the three head-subcluster sums and their ratios/fractions
was a wash-to-marginal gain (0.8717 vs 0.8710) and was kept.

WHY IT WORKS. The signal is compositional, not level-based. x_004/x_006 alone has
univariate AUC 0.755 (inverted), while x_004 alone is 0.642 and x_006 alone is 0.607 -- the
ratio is far stronger than either component, i.e. what predicts the target is the MIX of
activity across the head sub-clusters, not its volume. x_005/x_006 (0.751), x_009/x_013
(0.722) and x_000/x_008 (0.728) behave the same way. Tree models cannot construct ratios of
two raw columns, which is why handing them over explicitly is worth ~2 AUC points.

MODELS. Shallow trees dominated (num_leaves=4 > 8 > 16), consistent with a mostly-additive
signal in ratio space, and low colsample (0.08) helped given ~180 near-duplicate ratio
columns. Final = equal-weight rank average of four seed-bagged families: (a) LGBM on
raw+head-ratios+group-sums (205 cols, 8 seeds), (b) LGBM on a second, differently-engineered
264-col space (8 seeds), (c) ExtraTrees (4 seeds), (d) RandomForest (3 seeds), all trained
on all 5,000 research rows. Logistic regression on quantile-transformed features (0.861) was
tested and DROPPED: it was the worst member under both the plain and the shift-corrected CV
metric. Seed-bagged 3x5-fold CV of the exact final pipeline: 0.877.

CONFIRMATION LOOP. 3 calls, used only as blind sanity checks -- no model, feature set or
hyper-parameter was ever chosen on a confirmation score. Call 1, first ensemble without
head-ratios: 0.8276. Call 2, after adding head-ratios: 0.8431 (+0.0155, versus a +0.0136 CV
gain -- independent confirmation that the ratio discovery is real and not a CV fold
artifact). Call 3, final 4-family blend: 0.8391. Confirmation sits ~0.03 below CV
throughout; with ~55 expected positives in 1,500 rows the AUC standard error is ~0.03, so
both the level gap and the 0.004 call-2-vs-call-3 wobble are inside one standard error and I
deliberately did NOT switch back to the call-2 model on that basis.

ATTACK ON MY OWN APPROACH. Five lines of attack; one succeeded and changed the model.
(1) SUCCEEDED -- selection leakage. Ranking features by full-data gain importance and
keeping the top 40 "improved" 5x5 CV from 0.868 to 0.878. Re-running the selection strictly
inside each training fold destroyed the gain entirely: top-30 0.849, top-50 0.860, top-80
0.862, top-130 0.864 -- all WORSE than using all features. The 0.878 was pure selection
leakage. No feature selection is used in the final model.
(2) Confirmation-row overlap / oracle abuse. 20 of 1,500 confirmation rows and 22 of 1,500
transfer rows share an exact feature vector with a research row (~1.3%), too few to move a
1,500-row AUC, and I never fit anything to the confirmation labels (3 calls, all post-hoc).
(3) Duplicate-row leakage into real_test. 476 research rows have exact duplicates in
real_test, covering 11,341 test rows (2.2%). I checked whether this was exploitable: those
rows are sparse/default profiles with a 1.26% positive rate versus 3.93% elsewhere, and
within research the 33 duplicate groups are almost all all-negative -- a deterministic model
already scores identical feature vectors identically, so there is no extra signal here. Not
used.
(4) SPURIOUS-FEATURE CHECK on the ratio discovery. q(x_004/x_006) holds its sign and
strength in every tercile of x_102, x_015, x_103, x_104, x_000 and x_014 (subgroup AUCs
0.61-0.88, never near 0.5, never inverted), and its real_test quantiles (0, 1, 1.5, 4.76, 18)
essentially match research (0, 1, 1.5, 4.5, 15). It is not a pool-specific artifact.
(5) DISTRIBUTION SHIFT to real_test -- the one thing that genuinely worries me, and the
reason confirmation is a weak proxy for the real grade. Adversarial validation gives
research-vs-(confirmation+transfer) AUC 0.493, i.e. the three small sets are exchangeable
(so confirmation IS a fair proxy for transfer), but pool-vs-real_test AUC 0.673-0.679: the
8,000-row pool is NOT a random draw from real_test's population. Drivers are x_014, x_013,
x_004, x_007, x_105, x_103. Two concrete symptoms: ~0.4% of pool rows carry values orders of
magnitude beyond anything in 506,691 real_test rows (x_017 reaches 792 in research, max 18
in real_test), and x_007 is non-zero in 0.38% of pool rows versus 2.55% of real_test rows.
The gap is not explained by class enrichment -- solving for the real_test positive rate that
would reproduce its x_014 mean from the research conditional means gives a negative rate.
I therefore built a density-ratio (importance) weight from the adversarial classifier
(ESS 2,615/5,000, weights clipped at the 99.5th pct) and re-ran CV with a shift-corrected
weighted AUC, which estimates real_test performance rather than pool performance. Results:
the unweighted-trained model scores 0.884 weighted vs 0.877 plain, so the shift does not
appear to hurt; and training WITH importance weights did not improve the weighted estimate
(0.8832 weighted-trained vs 0.8837 unweighted-trained), so I did not adopt weighting.
The weighted metric was also used as a second, independent tie-breaker when picking blend
members -- it is what killed the logistic-regression member (0.8525 weighted, clearly worst).
Caveat I want on record: the shift is real, the correction is only as good as the density
estimate, and confirmation AUC measures the pool distribution, not real_test's.

WHAT I'D FLAG. Everything after the head-ratio discovery is worth ~0.006 AUC and sits inside
seed noise; the honest summary is that one structural insight (compositional ratios in a
block of collinear head counts) carries the result, plus shallow trees, seed bagging, and
family diversity. real_test predictions come from exactly this pipeline, refit on all 5,000
research rows, rank-averaged across the four families within real_test.
